metadata.title: Colourful Holi Celebration with Indian/Pakistani Diaspora in Dubai I Dubai's Worship Village
metadata.description:
During our Dubai visit, since Holi was around the corner, our gracious hosts and friends had arranged a pre Holi party at one of their homes to make us witness festive fervour at a distant land. This festive gathering organised by Tulika and her family, who are the close friends of our hosts Sachin, Mona and Lalatendu, was going to be a conglomeration of close friends from different nationalities. 

The same morning we visited Worship Village in Jebel Ali, which houses nine shrines of different religions. We visited the Gurudwara and the newly built magnificent Hindu temple. The place conveys a message of tolerance, peace and harmony and brings together people from various faiths. 

Finally in the evening we left for the Holi party. But first we made a stop at Gangour Sweets to get the mandatory North Indian Holi things that were gujiya and gulal. There were a huge variety on display but we picked up the classic one. 

On reaching Tulika's house we received a smiling welcome from everyone who had gathered there. The lawn and the backyard were decorated with colourful lights and the whole atmosphere was all euphoric. Everyone was dressed in traditional attire. We were overjoyed to experience the mix of cultures as people from various nationalities joined in to embrace the spirit of Holi

Tulika was the sweetest hostess who ensured that we had the best time with her favourite people. She joyfully introduced us to everyone and the warmth was so endearing. 

First we had a hearty conversation with the menfolk about the festive fervour and then with the womenfolk. Everyone shared their stories with a sparkle of both joy and nostalgia in their eyes which touched our hearts. Although everyone from the Indian diaspora cherished the sea of memories from back home, they are weaving new ones here in Dubai which is now their new abode. They were all praises about the multi-cultural diversity of this country. 

After smearing each other with colours we made our way to the dining area where a buffet was set up by one of Dubai's noted Indian restaurants. The thoughtful menu included Bihari mutton, dal, rice, dahi bhalle, salad, malpua, gulab jamun shrikhand etc. With the perfect balance of spices, tender mutton pieces and the kick of mustard oil, the Bihari mutton was our favourite. Everything else was delicious too. After the meal we had some yummy homemade gujiya. 

This celebration of Holi with the Indian diaspora and other nationals in Dubai was an opportunity to the power of celebrations to bring people together and promote unity in a multicultural society



About the host:

https://anubhavsapra.com/
